title: Government Representation
description: Assignment profiles of governments under the comparative representation systems: country name -> system -> characteristic element -> value.

systems.description: Version of each representation system the profiles were read under.

countries.description: Keyed by country name; a country carries any subset of the systems.

submodel.description: The note's own characterisation system: an orthogonal decomposition of a well-functioning government-wide administration into 23 submodels, each carrying the dimensions that locate a system within its domain.

Coordination structure.description: Organizational arrangement through which administrative action is coordinated across government.

Coordination authority.description: Authority responsible for initiating, directing, and maintaining cross-government coordination.

Coordination intensity.description: Extent to which participating organizations coordinate their administrative activities.

Conflict resolution.description: Mechanisms used to resolve disagreements between administrative organizations.

Participation requirements.description: Extent to which administrative organizations are required to participate in coordination arrangements.

Functional allocation.description: Distribution of government-wide administrative functions among central authorities and participating organizations.

Functional concentration.description: Degree to which responsibility for a function is concentrated in a single organization or distributed across several organizations.

Functional specialization.description: Extent to which administrative organizations specialize in particular government-wide functions.

Functional autonomy.description: Degree of discretion organizations have over the execution of their assigned administrative functions.

Functional overlap.description: Extent to which administrative responsibilities overlap between institutions or organizations.

Functional coverage.description: Extent to which the administrative system assigns responsibility for the relevant government-wide functions.

Career and employment system.description: General arrangement through which public personnel enter, remain in, and progress through government employment.

Recruitment system.description: Principal arrangements for recruiting personnel into administrative positions.

Selection authority.description: Organizational level responsible for selecting personnel.

Employment security.description: Degree and basis of employment protection for public personnel.

Career progression.description: Principal mechanism through which personnel advance to higher positions or grades.

Personnel mobility.description: Extent to which personnel can move between government organizations and occupational groups.

Remuneration system.description: How salaries and related compensation are determined across government.

Senior executive system.description: Arrangements governing the recruitment, appointment, development, and management of senior administrators.

Institutional configuration.description: Distribution of government-wide administrative responsibilities among institutions and administrative bodies.

Institutional mandate.description: Degree to which the responsibilities and jurisdiction of each institution are formally defined.

Institutional autonomy.description: Degree of organizational independence enjoyed by administrative institutions.

Institutional specialization.description: Extent to which institutions have distinct functional mandates.

Institutional hierarchy.description: Formal hierarchical relationships among institutions responsible for government-wide administration.

Institutional stability.description: Degree of continuity in the system's institutional configuration.

Decision-making authority.description: Distribution of formal authority to make administrative decisions.

Delegation arrangements.description: Rules and practices governing the transfer of decision-making authority to subordinate or participating organizations.

Reserved powers.description: Decisions retained exclusively by central or designated authorities.

Rulemaking authority.description: Distribution of authority to establish administrative rules and binding standards.

Enforcement authority.description: Distribution of authority to enforce government-wide administrative requirements.

Discretion.description: Degree of freedom organizations have when applying common administrative requirements.

Review and appeal rights.description: Arrangements for reviewing administrative decisions and challenging their application.

Institutional integration.description: Extent to which administrative institutions operate through connected governance and organizational arrangements.

Procedural integration.description: Extent to which administrative procedures and workflows are coordinated across organizations.

Information integration.description: Extent to which administrative information is shared and usable across government organizations.

Technical interoperability.description: Ability of administrative information systems to exchange and process information.

Semantic interoperability.description: Extent to which organizations use compatible definitions, classifications, and meanings for shared information.

Integration governance.description: Arrangements for setting priorities, standards, and responsibilities for system-wide integration.

Administrative standardization.description: Extent to which common administrative rules, procedures, classifications, and standards apply across government.

Standardization scope.description: Range of organizations, functions, and processes covered by common standards.

Standard-setting authority.description: Authority responsible for establishing common administrative standards.

Binding force.description: Degree to which common standards are legally or administratively mandatory.

Permitted variation.description: Extent to which organizations may deviate from common administrative standards.

Exception management.description: Procedures for requesting, authorizing, documenting, and reviewing exceptions to common standards.

Control mechanisms.description: Principal mechanisms through which authorities influence and monitor administrative organizations.

Ex ante control.description: Extent to which decisions and transactions require approval or verification before execution.

Ex post control.description: Extent to which completed decisions and activities are reviewed for compliance and performance.

Control locus.description: Organizational level at which administrative control is primarily exercised.

Corrective authority.description: Authority to require corrective action when administrative deficiencies are identified.

Sanctioning capacity.description: Ability to impose consequences for noncompliance or administrative misconduct.

Risk orientation.description: Extent to which control activities are prioritized according to assessed risks.

Shared-service provision.description: Organizational arrangement through which common administrative services are delivered.

Service ownership.description: Institution responsible for defining service requirements and overseeing service delivery.

Service delivery location.description: Where common administrative services are operationally performed.

Service coverage.description: Range of organizations eligible or required to use shared administrative services.

Service financing.description: How shared administrative services are financed.

Service-level governance.description: How service quality, responsibilities, costs, and delivery expectations are agreed and monitored.

Outsourcing arrangements.description: Extent to which administrative service delivery is assigned to external providers.

Rulemaking and regulation.description: How government-wide administrative rules and requirements are established and applied.

Regulatory scope.description: Range of administrative functions and organizations governed by common regulatory arrangements.

Regulatory hierarchy.description: Relationship between general administrative rules and function-specific or organization-specific requirements.

Regulatory coherence.description: Degree to which administrative rules are mutually consistent and compatible.

Regulatory discretion.description: Degree of freedom available to authorities when interpreting and applying administrative rules.

Rule revision.description: Mechanisms for reviewing, updating, consolidating, and repealing administrative rules.

Regulatory consultation.description: Extent to which affected organizations and stakeholders participate in developing administrative rules.

Accountability structure.description: Arrangement of relationships through which administrative organizations account for decisions, compliance, and results.

enum: Downward to service users or the public
Accountability direction.description: Direction in which administrative organizations and officials are required to account for their actions.

Accountability scope.description: Matters for which administrative actors are required to provide explanations or accept responsibility.

Reporting obligations.description: Requirements to submit administrative, financial, compliance, or performance information.

Oversight independence.description: Degree of independence enjoyed by bodies responsible for reviewing administrative conduct.

Transparency obligations.description: Requirements to disclose administrative information to oversight bodies and the public.

Complaint and redress.description: Mechanisms through which individuals and organizations can challenge administrative decisions or service failures.

Remedial follow-through.description: Extent to which findings from audits, investigations, and reviews result in corrective action.

Digital infrastructure.description: Organization of the digital infrastructure supporting administrative operations across government.

Platform ownership.description: Allocation of ownership and operational responsibility for shared digital platforms.

Digital service architecture.description: Arrangement of digital platforms, applications, interfaces, and services across government.

Data stewardship.description: Allocation of responsibility for data quality, definitions, access, maintenance, and reuse.

Data-sharing authority.description: Rules governing whether and how administrative data can be exchanged across organizations.

Digital identity and access.description: Arrangement for identifying users and managing access to administrative systems.

Cybersecurity governance.description: Allocation of responsibility for setting and enforcing government-wide cybersecurity requirements.

Legacy-system dependence.description: Degree to which administrative operations depend on outdated or difficult-to-integrate systems.

Resource distribution.description: How funding, personnel, and technical resources for government-wide administrative functions are allocated.

Budgetary authority.description: Distribution of authority to propose, approve, reallocate, and control administrative budgets.

Funding predictability.description: Degree to which administrative organizations can anticipate the resources available to them.

Cost allocation.description: Method used to assign the costs of shared administrative functions to participating organizations.

Resource pooling.description: Extent to which organizations combine or share resources to support common administrative functions.

Procurement authority.description: Distribution of authority for acquiring goods and services used in government-wide administration.

Resource flexibility.description: Degree to which organizations can reallocate resources in response to changing administrative needs.

Administrative capacity distribution.description: Distribution of administrative expertise and implementation capacity across government.

Strategic capacity.description: Distribution of expertise for system-wide planning, policy development, and administrative reform.

Technical expertise.description: Availability and distribution of specialized professional and technical knowledge.

Leadership capacity.description: Distribution of leadership and senior management capabilities across administrative organizations.

Analytical capacity.description: Ability to collect, interpret, and use evidence for administrative decisions and improvement.

Capability development.description: Arrangements for developing and maintaining administrative competencies.

Capability equalization.description: Mechanisms for addressing differences in capability between organizations or levels of government.

Implementation responsibility.description: Allocation of responsibility for putting government-wide administrative policies and requirements into practice.

Implementation discretion.description: Degree of freedom organizations have to adapt common requirements during implementation.

Implementation sequencing.description: How implementation is scheduled across organizations and functions.

Implementation support.description: Assistance available to organizations implementing common administrative requirements.

Compliance variation.description: Degree to which organizations differ in their actual application of common requirements.

Implementation monitoring.description: Arrangements for tracking progress, identifying barriers, and verifying implementation.

Implementation incentives.description: Mechanisms used to encourage or secure implementation.

Institutional adaptability.description: Ability of the administrative system to respond to changing requirements and circumstances.

Reform initiation.description: Distribution of authority to identify and initiate administrative reforms.

Reform coordination.description: Arrangements for coordinating reform initiatives across government organizations.

Change velocity.description: Typical pace at which the system can approve and implement administrative changes.

Experimentation.description: Extent to which administrative organizations can test new approaches before wider adoption.

Reform reversibility.description: Ability to revise, discontinue, or reverse reforms when results are inadequate or circumstances change.

Institutional memory.description: Extent to which the system retains knowledge of previous reforms and organizational changes.

Performance management arrangements.description: Organization of the processes through which administrative performance is defined, measured, reviewed, and used.

Indicator standardization.description: Extent to which common definitions and indicators are used across administrative organizations.

Target setting.description: How administrative performance targets are established.

Performance reporting.description: Arrangements for reporting administrative results across government.

Evaluation independence.description: Degree to which performance assessments are independent of the organizations being assessed.

Performance consequences.description: Extent to which performance results influence administrative decisions and organizational behavior.

Benchmarking.description: Extent to which organizations compare administrative performance against common benchmarks or one another.

Evaluation and learning cycle.description: Extent to which performance evidence leads to review, corrective action, and subsequent reassessment.

Strategic steering authority.description: Authority responsible for setting the overall direction of government-wide administration.

Leadership configuration.description: Arrangement through which system-wide administrative leadership is exercised.

Priority alignment.description: Extent to which administrative organizations align their priorities with government-wide objectives.

Cross-government decision forums.description: Formal forums through which system-wide administrative decisions are discussed and made.

Strategic dispute resolution.description: Mechanisms for resolving competing priorities among administrative institutions.

Steering accountability.description: Arrangements for holding system-wide leaders and steering bodies accountable for their direction and decisions.

Planning horizon.description: Time period explicitly considered in government-wide administrative planning.

Administrative strategy.description: Extent to which government-wide administration is guided by an explicit strategic framework.

Priority setting.description: Process through which administrative development priorities are identified and ranked.

Planning integration.description: Degree to which administrative plans align with fiscal plans, workforce plans, digital strategies, and wider government objectives.

Planning participation.description: Extent to which administrative organizations and affected stakeholders contribute to strategic planning.

Plan-to-budget linkage.description: Degree to which administrative plans influence budget allocations and resource commitments.

Strategic review.description: Frequency and method by which administrative priorities and plans are reassessed.

Process architecture.description: How government-wide administrative workflows and procedures are structured.

Process ownership.description: Allocation of responsibility for the design, operation, and improvement of administrative processes.

Workflow integration.description: Degree to which processes connect activities across organizational boundaries.

Process standardization.description: Extent to which common process designs and procedures are used across organizations.

Process automation.description: Extent to which administrative processes are automated through digital systems.

Process performance.description: Extent to which process efficiency, timeliness, cost, and error rates are systematically measured.

Process redesign.description: Arrangements for simplifying, reengineering, and improving administrative workflows.

Ethics framework.description: Existence and scope of common ethical principles and conduct requirements for public administration.

Conflict-of-interest management.description: Arrangements for identifying, disclosing, preventing, and managing conflicts of interest.

Anti-corruption coordination.description: Organization of responsibilities for preventing and addressing corruption across government.

Whistleblowing protection.description: Legal and administrative protections and reporting channels for individuals who report misconduct.

Integrity oversight.description: Arrangements for monitoring compliance with ethics and integrity requirements.

Disciplinary arrangements.description: How misconduct is investigated, adjudicated, and sanctioned across government.

Integrity risk management.description: Extent to which corruption and ethical risks are systematically identified and mitigated.

Territorial coverage.description: Levels of government included in the administrative system's jurisdiction or coordination arrangements.

Subnational administrative autonomy.description: Degree of discretion exercised by subnational authorities over administrative arrangements.

Intergovernmental coordination.description: Arrangements for coordinating administrative policies and practices across territorial levels.

Administrative standards reach.description: Extent to which government-wide administrative standards apply across territorial levels.

Fiscal-administrative linkage.description: Relationship between resource transfers and administrative responsibilities across levels of government.

Capacity equalization.description: Arrangements for addressing differences in administrative capability across territorial governments.

Intergovernmental dispute resolution.description: Mechanisms for resolving administrative disputes between territorial levels of government.

Knowledge management.description: Arrangements for documenting, organizing, and making administrative knowledge available across government.

Knowledge retention.description: Extent to which administrative records, precedents, decisions, and lessons survive personnel turnover and institutional change.

Knowledge sharing.description: Extent to which administrative organizations exchange expertise, lessons, and effective practices.

Lessons-learned processes.description: Mechanisms for identifying and applying lessons from implementation, audits, evaluations, and administrative failures.

Professional learning networks.description: Arrangements for connecting administrative professionals across organizations to exchange knowledge and expertise.

Evidence use.description: Extent to which research, administrative data, evaluations, and operational evidence inform administrative decisions.

Knowledge transfer.description: Arrangements for transferring expertise and administrative knowledge between organizations, roles, and generations of personnel.

structural-configuration.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by the shape of its organization: how differentiated, how layered, how formalized, and how autonomous its units are.

Functional specialization.description: Degree to which administrative units are differentiated by specialized function.

Vertical differentiation.description: Number of hierarchical levels separating top authority from operating units.

Horizontal differentiation.description: Number of distinct organizational units or functions coexisting at the same level.

Span of control.description: Number of subordinates reporting to a typical supervisor.

Formalization.description: Extent to which rules, procedures, and roles are written and prescribed.

Procedural standardization.description: Extent to which like activities follow common prescribed procedures.

Centralization of authority.description: Locus of decision-making authority in the hierarchy.

Line-staff balance.description: Relative weight of line authority versus staff and advisory units.

Administrative intensity.description: Proportion of administrative and managerial staff relative to operating staff.

Professionalization.description: Extent to which staff hold formal professional qualifications.

system-properties.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by graded system-wide qualities, as spectra rather than types.

Centralization.description: Concentration of authority and coordination in centers versus agencies.

Standardization.description: Extent of common procedures, rules, and requirements.

Integration.description: Cross-boundary linkage of functions and processes.

Sharing.description: Central or joint versus replicated service provision.

Interoperability.description: Cross-boundary capacity of systems and data.

Discretion.description: Freedom in applying common administrative requirements.

Formalization.description: Degree to which arrangements are legally or administratively prescribed.

Coordination intensity.description: Frequency and intensity of cross-organization coordination.

Transparency.description: Public accessibility of decisions, information, and operations.

Predictability.description: Stability and anticipability of rules and resourcing.

Adaptability.description: Capacity of the system to change its arrangements.

function-allocation.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by where each core administrative function is performed along the center-agency axis.

Budgeting function.description: Where budget formulation, allocation, and control are performed.

Accounting function.description: Where accounting and financial reporting are performed.

Human resource function.description: Where public-employment and workforce management are performed.

Procurement function.description: Where public procurement and asset management are performed.

Records and information function.description: Where records management and information exchange are performed.

Digital and information function.description: Where common information systems and digital platforms are operated.

Legal and regulatory function.description: Where administrative-rule drafting and interpretation are performed.

Audit and inspection function.description: Where auditing, inspecting, and review are performed.

Performance-evaluation function.description: Where administrative performance is defined, measured, and used.

decision-rights.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by who holds authority over each class of administrative decision.

Agenda-setting authority.description: Who sets the government-wide administrative agenda.

Rulemaking authority.description: Who establishes administrative rules and binding standards.

Resource-allocation authority.description: Who allocates administrative budgets and resources.

Staffing authority.description: Who selects and appoints administrative personnel.

Execution authority.description: Who implements administrative policies and requirements.

Review and appeal authority.description: Who hears challenges to administrative decisions.

wwbi-employment-profile.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by the demographics of its public workforce, using the indicator families of the World Bank Worldwide Bureaucracy Indicators.

Public-employment share.description: Public sector share of total employment.

Public-employment size.description: Absolute size of the public workforce.

Female representation.description: Share of women in public employment.

Female-male employment ratio.description: Balance of women to men in public employment.

Age structure.description: Distribution of public employees across age groups.

Education composition.description: Educational attainment profile of public employees.

Occupational composition.description: Distribution of public employees across occupations.

Industry composition.description: Distribution of public employees across sectors.

Income-quintile composition.description: Distribution of public employees across household income quintiles.

Formality.description: Share of public employment that is formal.

wwbi-compensation-profile.description: Locates a government-wide administrative system by how its public workforce is paid, using the indicator families of the World Bank Worldwide Bureaucracy Indicators.

Public-private wage premium.description: Competitiveness of public versus private sector wages.

Pay compression ratio.description: Ratio of top to bottom pay within the public sector.

Education wage differential.description: Public pay differential by education level.

Gender pay gap.description: Public-sector pay gap between women and men.

Income-quintile wage differential.description: Pay differential across household income quintiles within the public sector.

Wage-bill size.description: Public sector wage bill relative to GDP or expenditure.

Wage-bill affordability.description: Fiscal affordability of the public wage bill.
